title: Hotset contention simulator for KV cache: tokens/sec & p95 regression harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: build a deterministic, configurable workload simulator that stresses KV/prefix cache hotsets and multi-tenant contention so we can quantify tokens/sec, p95 latency degradation, and memory vs hit-rate tradeoffs under realistic temporal locality shifts. This harness will power both continuous regression detection and targeted experiments for eviction/TTL policy changes. Motivation: existing fixtures focus on static hit-rate sweeps and single-tenant steady-state behavior. We need a workload generator that models hotset churn, bursty fanout (many small requests to a hot prefix), tenant noise (background traffic), and pattern shifts (hotset migration) so regressions caused by scheduling, background GC, or eviction path changes are detected before they reach production.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can reproduce configurable scenarios: hotset size, churn rate, tenant count, burst factor, and working set skew (zipf alpha) via CLI/config file
2) Metrics captured for each run: aggregate tokens/sec, per-shard p95/p50/p99 latencies, observed KV hit-rate, resident memory used, eviction rate, CPU% and GPU% (where applicable)
3) Regression detector produces a human-readable report and an anomaly score for tokens/sec and p95 with configurable sensitivity (z-score and EWMA options)
4) Reproducible artifact links are emitted to CI (s3 + perf dashboard URL) and a GitHub PR can attach the report automatically
5) Baseline run and a perturbation run can be compared with a single command and the harness highlights where p95 increased >20% or tokens/sec dropped >15% as actionable regressions
test_plan: Implement synthetic workload generator with configurable distributions: zipfian alpha, hotset_fraction, churn_rate (keys/sec), and burst_factor (requests per second spikes)
Add multi-tenant overlay: X tenants each with independent hotset parameters to simulate noisy neighbors
Support scheduled pattern changes: at t=T1 move hotset from shard A->B, at t=T2 double churn_rate to emulate a migration surge
Instrument runtime hooks: sample KV hit/miss at op granularity, export per-request trace ids for correlation with tokenization and model exec
Integrate with CI: baseline nightly job + regression detection alert if score > threshold, plus human-run debugging mode with flamegraph capture
Publish dashboard panels in Console (tokens/sec, p95 by shard, hit-rate vs memory contour)
regression_detection_strategy: Primary detectors: two-tier approach combining robust z-score on sample windows (default window = 12 samples of 1min) and change-point detection via EWMA+CUSUM for sustained shifts
Score composition: weighted aggregation of tokens/sec drop and p95 increase with tunable weights; by default weight_p95=0.6 weight_tps=0.4
False-positive mitigation: require persistence for >3 consecutive windows or corroborating increases in eviction rate or memory pressure
Alerting: CI job posts a summary to #perf-regressions Slack with a link to the report and the top 5 contributing traces
Telemetry retention: keep raw samples for 30 days in perf-s3 for forensic replays
harness_implementation_notes: Simulator will be implemented in Go for low overhead and deterministic scheduling; use go-zipf for hotset distributions
Use gRPC stream clients to mimic real inference request patterns and to capture per-request token counts
Shard-awareness: simulator can pin tenants to a set of shards to emulate uneven distribution; supports docker-compose + k8s manifests for target environments
Memory instrumentation uses jemalloc stats (where present) plus procfs RSS on Linux; we will correlate allocator metrics with eviction ops
Include a 'replay' mode that replays request event logs at original timestamps to reproduce contention scenarios exactly
initial_results_notes: Prototype run (local single-node, 8 tenants, hotset_fraction=0.05) revealed a non-linear p95 cliff when eviction_rate exceeded ~1200 ops/min — root cause likely lock contention in eviction path
Tokens/sec remained stable until eviction rate crossed threshold, then tokens/sec dropped ~18% while p95 jumped 40% for tail requests
Observed memory RSS plateau before eviction rate surge suggests delayed reclamation in allocator; need to instrument allocator arenas and run with tcmalloc for comparison
Preliminary regression detector correctly flagged the candidate run when tuned to require 3 windows persistence; with single-window sensitivity it produced false positives under short bursts
